clue.text: System maintaining speed in swirling current is cool

indicators.note: water that swirls churns round, so the words it describes are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: A cooling system that holds things steady by keeping a swirling flow moving at the right rate.
explanation.definitionFit: Cruise control is the car feature that holds a vehicle at a set speed without the driver touching the pedal.

clue.text: Protest about to be raised over variable entertainment

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising something lifts it so it reads from the bottom upward
in a down clue, a piece placed over another sits above it, so it comes first

blocks.note: c. is the abbreviation for circa, about
algebra uses x, y and z for unknowns or variables

explanation.surface: A demonstration is planned against some changeable piece of entertainment.
explanation.definitionFit: Comedy is a genre of light, amusing show, so it is one kind of entertainment.

clue.text: Song stirring audience, old hymn

indicators.note: stirring mixes things up, so the following letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: An old hymn moving a congregation emotionally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stirring' reads as an adjective praising the hymn; it is the mixing signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Unchained Melody is a famous 1955 song, best known in the Righteous Brothers' recording.

clue.text: Saint keeping lid on self-esteem, a fall guy

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece set on another sits above it and is read first
to keep something is to hold it inside, so the saint's letters wrap round the rest

blocks.note: a cap is a lid or top

explanation.surface: A holy man who keeps his pride in check ends up taking the blame.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lid on self-esteem' reads like keeping pride in check, but it is just two pieces stacked in order.
explanation.definitionFit: A fall guy is someone made to take the blame for others, which is what a scapegoat is.

clue.text: Desire firm check

blocks.note: Co. is the abbreviation for company, a firm
to vet is to check carefully

explanation.surface: A wish that a business would carry out a proper inspection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Firm' looks like an adjective describing the check; it is the noun, a company.
explanation.definitionFit: To covet is to desire something, especially what belongs to another.

clue.text: Lyrical pieces on sect run strangely

indicators.note: something run strangely is out of its normal order, so these letters get rearranged

blocks.note: also part of the fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: Song lyrics written about a religious group that is managed oddly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' does double work: it reads as joining the definition, but its letters are part of what is shuffled.
explanation.definitionFit: Nocturnes are dreamy, song-like piano pieces such as Chopin's, so they are lyrical pieces of music.

clue.text: Regular members of group really relating to countryside

indicators.note: taking members at regular intervals means picking every other letter

blocks.note: the second, fourth, sixth, eighth and tenth letters

explanation.surface: The usual members of a band are truly connected to rural life.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes things belonging to the country rather than the town, matching the phrase exactly.

clue.text: Working in field excited avid Nordic artist

indicators.note: one thing in another is placed inside it
excited things are agitated and stirred up, so the next letters are scrambled

blocks.note: a lea is a meadow or field, a crossword staple
a machine that is working is on

explanation.surface: A keen Scandinavian gets worked up while labouring out in the fields.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Working in field' reads as a farmhand's day; it is an insertion. Lea is a poetic word for a meadow.
explanation.definitionFit: Leonardo da Vinci was the Italian Renaissance painter of the Mona Lisa, the archetypal artist.

clue.text: Avoid extremes in encounters with champ

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its two ends, the first and last letters

blocks.note: to champ is to munch or chew noisily

explanation.surface: Advice to steer clear of the most dramatic moments in bouts against a champion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Champ' looks like a champion boxer; here it is the verb, as a horse champs at the bit.
explanation.definitionFit: To eschew something is to deliberately avoid or abstain from it.

clue.text: Coffee made by doctor before tea

indicators.note: one piece coming before another is placed ahead of it in the answer

blocks.note: cha (or char) is British slang for tea

explanation.surface: A medic brews a coffee before moving on to tea.
explanation.definitionFit: Mocha is a type of coffee, often flavoured with chocolate, named after the Yemeni port.

clue.text: Assorted clothing I start to collect, second-hand

indicators.note: clothing something wraps it, so these letters go round the others
the start of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A shopper starts gathering a mixed bag of second-hand clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: V(IC)ARIOUS: the two inserted letters go after the opening V. 'Clothing' looks like garments, but it is the verb, wrapping.
explanation.definitionFit: Vicarious experience is felt at second hand, through imagining someone else's life rather than living it.

clue.text: Form of language that's ideal ordered by court

indicators.note: putting letters in a new order rearranges them
by means beside, so the next piece is set alongside

blocks.note: CT is the abbreviation for court

explanation.surface: The perfect way of speaking, as decreed by a court of law.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ordered' reads as a judge's command; it signals rearranging.
explanation.definitionFit: A dialect is a regional variety of a language, with its own vocabulary and grammar.

clue.text: Relative losing heart has broken free

indicators.note: losing its heart means the centre letter of the word drops out
something broken comes apart and is put back in a different order

explanation.surface: A dispirited family member has escaped captivity.
explanation.walkthrough: UNCLE loses its central C, then the letters of 'has' are shuffled. 'Broken free' looks like one phrase, but 'free' alone is the definition, as a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To unleash is to release or let loose, so it means to free something held back.

clue.text: Finish changing most new gifts

indicators.note: changing the words alters their arrangement, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Wrapping up by swapping most of the new presents.
explanation.definitionFit: Endowments are natural talents or donated funds, both senses of things bestowed as gifts.

clue.text: Pack up old game to become traveller

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means reading from the bottom upward

blocks.note: to cram is to pack tightly
polo is a game played on horseback

explanation.surface: Someone packs away an outdated game and heads off on a journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pack up' reads as one phrase meaning to stop; only 'up' is the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Marco Polo was the Venetian merchant whose journeys to China in the 13th century made him a famous traveller.

clue.text: Delay in overtures to new alliance

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the run of words that follows

blocks.note: spans the end of the first word, two whole words and the start of the last

explanation.surface: Diplomatic approaches toward a fresh coalition are being held up.
explanation.definitionFit: To stonewall is to obstruct or delay, as with evasive answers or stalling play in cricket.

clue.text: Moisture expected by the sound of it

indicators.note: judging by sound means the word is spoken rather than spelt

explanation.surface: Damp weather that was forecast, so it seems.
explanation.definitionFit: Dew is the droplets of water that condense on cool surfaces overnight, a form of moisture.

clue.text: Invite offer

blocks.note: first meaning: to ask someone, as in the old phrase bidding guests to a feast
second meaning: a price put forward at an auction

explanation.walkthrough: Read together the words sound like extending an invitation; they are two separate meanings of one short word.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb has an old sense of summon or invite, and the noun is an offer of a price at auction.

clue.text: Happen to absorb arguments read casually

indicators.note: to absorb something is to take it inside, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: to be is to exist or happen
a row (rhymes with cow) is a quarrel

explanation.surface: Arguments one happens to overhear are taken in while skimming the paper.
explanation.walkthrough: B(ROWS)E: the quarrels sit inside the two-letter verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To browse is to look through a book or shop without real purpose, skimming rather than studying.

clue.text: Front of rampart in the south contains points of entry

indicators.note: the front of a word is its first letter
one thing in another is placed inside it

explanation.surface: A southern fortification has its own gateways built in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Contains' looks like it signals an enclosure, but it simply gives a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: A threshold is the sill of a doorway, the spot where one steps in, so thresholds are points of entry.

clue.text: Attach light-emitting diode, getting confused

blocks.note: to add something is to attach it

explanation.surface: Someone fitting a little electronic light gets baffled by the wiring.
explanation.definitionFit: Addled describes a muddled, befuddled mind, so it is a synonym of confused.

clue.text: Nothing right, for example, with a refusal to supply herb

explanation.surface: A grocer turns down a request for seasoning: nothing at all is right.
explanation.definitionFit: Oregano is an aromatic herb of the mint family, much used in Italian and Greek cooking.

clue.text: Just missing line?  That's terrible

indicators.note: a word missing something has had that part taken out

blocks.note: just in the sense of fair and legal

explanation.surface: An actor dries on stage: forgetting a single line is dreadful.
explanation.walkthrough: LAWFUL without its L. 'Just' looks like 'merely'; it is the adjective meaning fair or lawful.
explanation.definitionFit: Awful means very bad or dreadful, a direct synonym of terrible.

clue.text: Satisfied about weight, went off course

indicators.note: one thing about another goes round it

blocks.note: to serve a need is to satisfy it

explanation.surface: A contented traveller, mulling over their weight, strayed from the route.
explanation.walkthrough: S(W)ERVED: the weight goes inside the word for satisfied.
explanation.definitionFit: To swerve is to veer suddenly aside, so swerved means went off course.

clue.text: Abandon stunted vegetation

blocks.note: first meaning: to cancel or drop a plan, informally
second meaning: low, scrubby bushes and small trees

explanation.walkthrough: Read together it sounds like giving up on a poor patch of garden; the two parts are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb is slang for cancelling something, and the noun names land covered in low bushes.

clue.text: Puzzle behind quiet work in part of factory

indicators.note: something behind the rest comes after it, so this piece goes last

blocks.note: op. is short for opus, a work
to floor someone is to baffle them

explanation.surface: A conundrum quietly worked on at the back of the factory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Puzzle' looks like a noun, but it is the verb, to baffle.
explanation.definitionFit: The shop floor is the production area of a factory where the workers make things.

clue.text: Reverse in channel unnavigable to the west

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the run of words that follows
in an across clue, heading west means reading right to left

blocks.note: the last letter of the first word and the first four of the second

explanation.surface: A ship turns back in a waterway too shallow to pass westward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reverse' looks like a ship backing up, but it is the definition, in its legal sense.
explanation.definitionFit: To annul a decision or marriage is to cancel it officially, which is reversing it.

clue.text: Fearful shout, one's first, will be adjusted by editor

indicators.note: the first of a word is its opening letter
adjusting something rearranges it, so these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A nervous writer's draft cry will be corrected by the editor.
explanation.definitionFit: Yellow-bellied is an informal word for cowardly, so it describes someone fearful.
